correctness.rationale: Every graph vertex has degree N minus its part size. The unique smallest part is forced into every strongly dominating set; two repeated minimum parts allow a two-vertex solution. The resulting exact gamma formula is applied to all vertex-deletion cases, including the empty and one-part boundaries. All minimum witness classes and counts are exhaustive. The standalone direct verifier checks 183 complete multipartite profiles through order eleven and explicit twelve-vertex examples.

evidence: The primary source gives join claims as well as balanced-multipartite results.

A complete multipartite graph is an iterated join of edgeless graphs, but the printed two-vertex assertion for nonuniversal joins does not respect the degree requirement for a uniquely smallest part: the graph with part sizes (3,4,4) has strong domination number three.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general join statement, even if interpreted as covering this graph class, does not soundly imply the exact theorem because its asserted cardinality is contradicted by direct neighborhood and degree comparisons. No independently verified stronger result was found.

evidence: In the cited versions, the balanced size-three cases and the general balanced-case lower bounds are discussed.
Deleting one vertex from a minimum part of K_{4,4,4} yields K_{3,4,4}; its unique smallest part must be fully selected in any strong dominating set, so the parameter rises from two to three.
For K_{3,3,3}, a deletion of two vertices in one part produces a singleton universal vertex; no one-vertex deletion changes the minimum from two.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: These contradictions are checked at the level of the mathematical predicates, not paper titles. The prior propositions are neither a valid stronger coverage of this theorem nor ignored: they are treated explicitly as overlapping but inconsistent claims, and the final proof does not depend on them.

Searches of equivalent phrases, joins, tables, and closely related domination variants did not identify covering true statements. Later corrections and alternate indexing remain risks.

value.rationale: The vertex-deletion robustness of a natural domination invariant is determined for every multipartite size profile, with all minimum repair/disruption choices explicitly classified and counted. The sharp repeated-three anomaly and singleton-multiplicity threshold identify structural robustness regimes invisible from the original domination number. The result gives a concrete complete answer rather than a parameter substitution or a single small case.
